public_rationale: Ars Technica's June 16, 2026 report on audited statements gives calendar-2024 revenue of $3.7 billion and R&D expense alone of $7.81 billion [e3]. This supports several billion dollars in revenue and substantially greater company expenses, but does not identify cash outlays [e3]. CNBC's September 27, 2024 figures were projections for that year, not completed-year results [e1]. Reuters reported about 10 million paying ChatGPT users and projected $2.7 billion in 2024 ChatGPT revenue, without matching application costs [e2]. The later report also puts company-wide 2024 cost of revenue below revenue, but provides no application-level allocation of full costs [e3]. These sources therefore do not settle whether an application earned enough to justify its attributable costs, leaving the full claim unresolved [e2, e3].
limitations: Contemporary annual figures were projections [e1, e2].
The audited statements are described through news reporting rather than directly inspected [e3].
Reported accounting expenses do not settle the claim's unspecified outlay basis [e3].
Paid adoption, company losses and company gross margin do not establish application-level returns after attributable costs [e2, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's revenue (on the order of $5B) has been modest compared with much greater outlays, and no actual killer app, relative to the costs, has emerged.

statement.excerpt: Meanwhile, revenue (order of $5B) has been modest, compared to outlays that have been much greater; no actual killer app (relative to the costs) has emerged.
statement.document_title: The race for "AI Supremacy" is over — at least for now.

from_speaker: outlays that have been much greater
no actual killer app (relative to the costs) has emerged
our_interpretation: I use calendar 2024, the latest completed annual period before the post, because the surrounding comparison concerns annual company revenue and spending.
Order of $5B means approximately several billion dollars, not an exact $5 billion threshold.
Revenue means revenue earned over the year, rather than an annualized run rate.
Outlays means company spending, but Marcus does not specify cash payments, operating expenses, or another accounting measure.

A killer app relative to costs means an application with commercial returns sufficient to justify its attributable costs. Company-wide losses alone cannot establish the absence of such an application.
The supplied text does not attribute the figures or identify their accounting basis, so the contract basis remains unknown.
Relative to the costs qualifies the observation; it is not a forecast antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable calendar-2024 financial records show revenue of several billion dollars and substantially greater outlays, while application-level revenue and attributable costs establish the absence of a commercially justifying application.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records refute the revenue scale or spending gap, or establish an application whose commercial returns justify its attributable costs.
